newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zambia to privatise country's largest foundry.
newsitem.headline: Zambia to privatise country's largest foundry.

text.p: The Zambia Privatisation Agency said on Thursday it was inviting bids for the acquisition of 98.47 percent of Scaw Ltd, the country's largest foundry with a production capacity of over 18,000 tonnes a year.
In an advertisement in the South African press, the ZPA said it aimed to conclude negotiations with the lead bidder by the end of August this year.
Scaw's core business is the production of mill balls for the mining industry. Its other product lines are steel and iron castings. It employs 650 staff.
The company is a subsidiary of Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd, itself the subject of the country's biggest privatisation to date.
